mainTopic: The measure for returning to destroy חמץ, אגדה on זכריה's prophecies of the future and the Name of ה', and the opening משנה of מקום שנהגו on working on ערב פסח
overview: This amud opens by finishing the גמרא's explanation of רבי יהודה: the amount of חמץ that obligates you to go back home and destroy it is a כזית, the same amount the Torah forbids. A ברייתא adds רבי נתן's view of two eggs, which the חכמים reject. The גמרא then turns to אגדה on verses from זכריה about the future. 'יקרות וקפאון' gets three readings, and a story follows about רב יוסף's near-death vision of an upside-down world, where Torah scholars keep their standing and the הרוגי לוד stand on a level no one can reach. Next, 'מצלות הסוס' gets three readings, and the גמרא shows that the nearby verses fit all of them, with a side proof that כנעני can mean merchant. It then explains 'ה' will be one and His name one': in עולם הבא there will be only the blessing הטוב והמטיב, and the Name will be read as it is written. A short discussion follows on keeping the Name's pronunciation hidden. The amud closes פרק אלו עוברין and opens פרק מקום שנהגו, whose משנה teaches that working on ערב פסח until חצות follows local custom, and that a traveler keeps the stricter customs of both places.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reason: going back is measured like the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its explanation of רבי יהודה. Since the Torah forbids חמץ at the size of a כזית, a person must also go back home to destroy it once there is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Going back is] like its prohibition. Just as its prohibition is with an olive-size, so too going back for it is with an olive-size.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts mid-sentence. The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why רבי יהודה in the משנה says a person must go back home for as little as a כזית of חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ties two rules together. The amount that obligates you to return home equals the amount the Torah forbids you to own or eat, and that amount is a כזית. This is a simple 'match the measurements' approach. It contrasts with רבי מאיר, who uses a כביצה.

keyTerms.meaning: its prohibition (the amount the Torah forbids)
its returning (the obligation to go back home to destroy it)
an olive-size, the standard minimum measure for a forbidden food
'just as ... so too', a formula for making a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: The word כאיסורו at the very start is the tail end of a sentence that began on the previous amud ('רבי יהודה holds that going back is like its prohibition'). It is not a new opening.

phrases.english: [Its returning is] like its prohibition:
phrases.notes: This finishes the last line: רבי יהודה holds חזרתו כאיסורו, that its returning is like its prohibition.

phrases.english: just as its prohibition is with an olive-size,
so too its returning is with an olive-size.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּאִיסּוּרוֹ: מָה אִיסּוּרוֹ בִּכְזַיִת, אַף חֲזָרָתוֹ בִּכְזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation, begun on the previous עמוד, of the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה measures the obligation to return by the amount the Torah forbids, which is a כזית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must go back home to destroy חמץ (or קדשים meat) once there is a כזית.

steps.title: רבי נתן's opinion: two egg-sizes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי נתן, who says a person must go back for either case (חמץ or קדשים meat) only when there is two eggs' worth. The חכמים did not accept this.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says that both this and that are measured at two egg-sizes. The Sages did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with a fourth opinion on the amount. רבי נתן says two eggs, and the חכמים reject his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already had three views: רבי מאיר says a כביצה for both, רבי יהודה says a כזית for both, and the חכמים split (holy meat a כזית, חמץ a כביצה). רבי נתן adds a fourth: two כביצים for both. 'זה וזה' means one measurement covers both cases, and 'ולא הודו לו חכמים' tells us his opinion is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: this and that (both cases: חמץ and קדשים meat)
and the Sages did not agree with him

steps.whatToRemember: The opinions on when you must turn back: רבי מאיר says a כביצה, רבי יהודה says a כזית, the חכמים of the משנה say a כזית for holy meat and a כביצה for חמץ, and רבי נתן says two כביצים. The חכמים reject רבי נתן.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
this and that are two egg-sizes,
phrases.notes: Both the חמץ and the holy meat.

phrases.english: and the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth opinion on the same measurement question that רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נתן, the amount is two egg-sizes for both cases. The חכמים reject this.

steps.title: A verse about 'that day': what does 'יקרות וקפאון' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves into אגדה. It quotes a verse in זכריה about the future and asks what the unusual words 'יקרות וקפאון' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it shall be on that day, there will not be light, יקרות וקפאון.' What is 'יקרות וקפאון'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the halachic topic and begins a new aggadic discussion. It quotes a נבואה and asks about two hard words, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'יקרות וקפאון' are unclear, so the גמרא asks for their meaning. The question opens a series of teachings about the future world. This is a new subject, not a challenge to anything said earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: precious or heavy things (the word being explained)
and thickness or congealing (the word being explained)

phrases.english: "And it shall be on that day
there shall not be light,
precious and congealed."
What is "yekarot vekippaon"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A topic shift from the halachic measurement debate to an aggadic explanation of a נבואה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'יקרות וקפאון' in the verse.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: precious now, insignificant in the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the verse refers to the light of the sun. It is precious in עולם הזה but will count for little in עולם הבא, when everything shines far brighter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: This is the light that is precious in this world and of little worth in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by reading each hard word as a description of light. 'יקרות' means precious now, and 'קפאון' means of little worth later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the words as a play on meaning: יקר means precious, and קפוי means floating or cheap, like something of little value. The point is that today's sunlight, which we treasure, will seem minor in עולם הבא compared with the greater light of that time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
this is light that is precious in this world,
and of little worth in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: זֶה אוֹר שֶׁיָּקָר בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question about the meaning of the verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'יקרות וקפאון' describes light that is precious in עולם הזה and of little worth in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The verse refers to the topics of נגעים and אהלות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains 'יקרות וקפאון' as the topics נגעים and אהלות. They are hard in this world but will be easy in the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This refers to נגעים and אהלות. They are 'heavy' (hard) in this world, and they will be 'light' (easy) in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the verse. This one comes from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן keeps the same pattern as רבי אלעזר: something 'יקר' now that becomes 'קפוי' later. But for him it is about Torah topics. נגעים and אהלות are among the hardest areas of Torah to learn today, and in עולם הבא they will feel easy because people will understand much more.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of צרעת (skin afflictions); also the name of a מסכתא
Laws of טומאת מת spreading through a covering or tent; also a מסכתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
These are Nega'im and Oholos,
phrases.notes: Two of the hardest topics in סדר טהרות

phrases.english: which are heavy (difficult) in this world,
and are light (easy) in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵלּוּ נְגָעִים וְאֹהָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 3, offered alongside רבי אלעזר's answer in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יקרות וקפאון = נגעים and אהלות: hard now, easy in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: The verse refers to people honored here but low there
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains the verse as people who are important in this world but unimportant in the World to Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: These are people who are important in this world and unimportant in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation, from רבי יהושע בן לוי. This one is about people's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same two words now describe people. Someone may be 'יקר' (honored) in this world because of money or power. In the next world that honor does not count, and the person is 'קפוי' (low). This view prepares for the story that comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'קפויין' means 'unimportant,' not 'easy' as in רבי יוחנן's view. The same word gets a different meaning in each explanation.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
These are people
who are important in this world,
and are unimportant in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel answer to the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יקרות וקפאון = people honored in עולם הזה who are low in עולם הבא.

steps.title: The story of רב יוסף's near-death vision of an upside-down world
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, son of רבי יהושע בן לוי, almost died. He saw a world where the high were low and the low were high. His father said he had seen the true world.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the story of רב יוסף, son of רבי יהושע בן לוי. He became sick and nearly died. When he recovered, his father asked him: What did you see? He said: I saw an upside-down world. The ones on top were below, and the ones below were on top. His father said: My son, you saw a clear (true) world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that illustrates רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation. רב יוסף tells what he saw when he nearly died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי הא' ('like this') show that the story supports the previous view. People who were 'on top' here, the יקרין, were low there, and the lowly were raised. His father explains that this is not a confused world. It is the real one, where people are judged truly.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this (introduces a supporting case or story)
Became sick and nearly died (lost consciousness)

phrases.english: Like this incident of Rav Yosef,
son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
who became ill and was near death (his soul nearly left him),
When he recovered, his father said to him:
What did you see?
He said to him: I saw an upside-down world,
the high ones were below, and the low ones were above.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, עוֹלָם בָּרוּר רָאִיתָ.
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, you saw a clear (true) world.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports רבי יהושע בן לוי's explanation from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that people honored here are low in עולם הבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's near-death vision of an upside-down world

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks where Torah scholars stand there
steps.stepSummary: Inside the story, רבי יהושע בן לוי asks his son what the standing of Torah scholars like themselves is in that world.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we (Torah scholars), how are we there?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a question. The father asks where people like them, תלמידי חכמים, stand in that world. This sets up the son's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything is turned over in the next world, maybe the honor that Torah scholars get here is also reversed. The father wants to know whether their status holds up.

phrases.english: And we, how are we (regarded) there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question inside the story, prompted by the 'upside-down world.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the honor given to תלמידי חכמים in this world is also reversed in the next.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Torah scholars keep the same standing there
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that Torah scholars are regarded there just as they are here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we are here, so are we there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers his father. Torah scholars keep their honor in the next world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reversal applies to honor that comes from worldly things. Honor that comes from Torah is real, so it does not flip. This is why the father could call it a 'עולם ברור.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that only true value, such as Torah, keeps its worth in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Just as we are here,
so are we there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Torah scholars keep the same standing in עולם הבא as here.

steps.title: רב יוסף reports two sayings he heard in the next world
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף heard two sayings there. Fortunate is one who arrives with his learning in hand. And no one can stand in the place of those killed by the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I heard them saying: Fortunate is one who comes here with his learning in his hand. And I heard them saying: Those killed by the government, no person can stand in their area.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds two more things he heard in that world. One praises Torah learning, and one praises martyrs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first saying praises someone who arrives with his Torah learning remembered and with him. The second says martyrs have such a high level that no one else can stand in their section. The second saying sets up the גמרא's next question about who these martyrs are.

keyTerms.meaning: His learning in his hand (remembered and with him)
Those killed by the (Roman) government; martyrs

phrases.english: And I heard that they were saying:
Fortunate is one who comes here
with his learning in his hand.
And I heard that they were saying:
Those killed by the government —
no person can stand in their section.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: אַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁבָּא לְכָאן וְתַלְמוּדוֹ בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's report with two more sayings from the next world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arriving with one's Torah learning is praised, and martyrs have an unmatched level.

steps.title: Who are these martyrs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which martyrs רב יוסף meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks its own question about the story: who are the 'martyrs' that no one can stand next to? This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הרוגי מלכות' is general, so the גמרא wants to know exactly which group is meant.

phrases.english: (And) who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the הרוגי מלכות mentioned in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the הרוגי מלכות who have an unmatched level.

steps.title: It cannot mean רבי עקיבא and his colleagues
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי עקיבא and his friends and rejects it. Their greatness was not only because they were martyred.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means רבי עקיבא and his friends: is their greatness only because they were killed by the government, and nothing else?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer and immediately pushes back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא and his friends were giants in Torah and holiness all their lives. Saying their high level comes from being martyred, 'ותו לא' (and nothing more), would sell them short. So the saying must mean someone whose main greatness came from the martyrdom itself.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion about to be rejected)
רבי עקיבא and his colleagues (the עשרה הרוגי מלכות)

phrases.english: If you say Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues —
is it because they were killed by the government and nothing more?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to step 11 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the martyrs are רבי עקיבא and his colleagues
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their exalted level comes from their whole lives of Torah and holiness, not only from martyrdom, so the saying would not single out martyrdom for them.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the הרוגי מלכות in רב יוסף's report are רבי עקיבא and his colleagues
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their exalted level comes from whole lives of Torah and holiness, so it would be belittling to attribute it to martyrdom alone ('ותו לא').

steps.title: Conclusion: It means the הרוגי לוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the martyrs meant are the הרוגי לוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the martyrs of לוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the saying refers to the הרוגי לוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רש"י explains that the הרוגי לוד were the brothers פפוס and לוליינוס. They falsely confessed to killing the king's daughter to save the whole Jewish community from a decree. They were not famous for great piety beforehand, so their unmatched level truly comes from the martyrdom itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The martyrs of לוד (פפוס and לוליינוס)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'יקרות וקפאון' has three explanations: the sun's light (רבי אלעזר), נגעים and אהלות (רבי יוחנן), and people honored here but low there (רבי יהושע בן לוי). רב יוסף's vision teaches that Torah scholars keep their standing, learning is praised, and the הרוגי לוד have a level no one can reach.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how great self-sacrifice for the community is: one act of martyrdom can raise a person to a level no one can stand beside.

phrases.english: Rather: the martyrs of Lod.
phrases.notes: רש"י says these are פפוס and לוליינוס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי עקיבא and his colleagues in step 12, gives the correct identification.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הרוגי מלכות in רב יוסף's report are the הרוגי לוד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The martyrs whose level is unmatched are the הרוגי לוד, whose greatness came from their self-sacrifice.

steps.title: What does 'the bells of the horses' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a verse from זכריה about the future and asks what the unclear phrase מצלות הסוס means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On that day there shall be upon the מצלות of the horses: Holy unto ה'.' What is 'מצלות הסוס'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new verse from זכריה and asks what one hard phrase in it means. This sets up the three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מצלות is unclear. It could come from צלצול (ringing, so 'bells') or from צל (shadow). The question opens the door to several different readings.

keyTerms.meaning: On that day. The future time of the redemption.
The unclear phrase being explained. It could mean the horse's bells or something about the horse's shadow.
Holy unto ה'. Set aside for holiness.
What is? A standard question word asking for the meaning of something.

phrases.english: "On that day there shall be
upon the bells of the horses: Holy unto the Lord."
What is 'metzillot hasus'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רב יוסף's report and the martyrs. Starts explaining a new verse from the same section of זכריה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase מצלות הסוס in זכריה 14:20.

steps.title: ירושלים will be expanded to half a day's ride
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads מצלות as 'shadow': in the future ירושלים will be so big that a horse can run across it the whole time it casts a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: In the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will add to ירושלים until a horse can run across it the whole time it casts a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the first answer. He says the phrase describes how huge ירושלים will become in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads מצלות from the word צל, shadow. A horse running from morning until midday, when its shadow shrinks away, still won't reach the end of the city. So the verse is a picture of the city's future size, not a reference to actual bells.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future. Something that will happen.
Casts a shadow. From צֵל, shadow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will
add on to Jerusalem
until it equals the distance a horse runs while casting a shadow.
phrases.notes: About half a day. From morning until midday, when the shadow disappears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מצלות means 'shadow'. ירושלים will be expanded to the distance a horse runs while it still casts a shadow.

steps.title: The horse's decorative bells will become holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads מצלות simply as bells. All the bells hung between a horse's eyes will be made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: All the bells that people hang on a horse between its eyes will be holy to ה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second, more literal answer. The verse really is talking about the bells on horses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads מצלות from צלצול, ringing. In the future even the ornaments on horses will be consecrated to the בית המקדש treasury as הקדש. Unlike רבי יהושע בן לוי, he is not talking about shadows or the size of the city.

keyTerms.meaning: Hang. People hang the bells on the horse.
Between its eyes. On the horse's forehead.
Something consecrated to the בית המקדש. This is what 'holy to ה'' means here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
All the bells that one hangs
phrases.notes: Here מצילות means bells, from the word for ringing.

phrases.english: on the horse between its eyes
will be holy to the Lord.
phrases.notes: They will be consecrated to the Temple treasury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question, disagreeing with רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מצלות means bells. The ornamental bells on horses will be consecrated.

steps.title: Spoils taken in half a day will become holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads מצלות as 'shadow' again. All the spoils ישראל take in the time a horse runs while casting a shadow (half a day) will be holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All the spoils that ישראל take, up to the time a horse runs and casts a shadow, will be holy to ה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third answer. The verse is about the spoils of war that ישראל will take in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהושע בן לוי, he reads מציל as 'casting a shadow', meaning half a day. But he uses it to measure time, not the size of ירושלים. Whatever ישראל plunder from their enemies in that half day will be consecrated to ה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to the time. Here, a time limit of half a day.

steps.whatToRemember: One unclear word, מצלות, gets three readings. רבי יהושע בן לוי: shadow, so ירושלים will be half a day's ride across. רבי אלעזר: bells, so horses' bells will be holy. רבי יוחנן: shadow, so spoils taken in half a day will be holy.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן use the exact same words, 'עד שהסוס רץ ומציל'. Do not mix them up. רבי יהושע בן לוי uses them to measure distance (how big ירושלים will be). רבי יוחנן uses them to measure time (how long the spoils count).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
All the spoils that the Jewish people take
phrases.notes: From the nations who wage war against them.

phrases.english: up to the time a horse runs and casts a shadow
will be holy to the Lord.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question in step 14. It shares רבי יהושע בן לוי's 'shadow' reading but applies it to time and spoils instead of distance.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מצלות refers to the horse's shadow, meaning half a day. All spoils taken in that span will be consecrated.

steps.title: The verse about the pots fits only the spoils opinion
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'the pots in ה׳'s house will be like basins' fits רבי יוחנן, who says all ביזה becomes holy. What does it mean for the other two opinions?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who said 'all the spoils that ישראל take' become holy. That is why the verse says: 'And the pots in the house of ה׳ shall be like the basins before the altar.' But according to the ones who gave the other two explanations, what does 'And the pots in the house of ה׳' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first two explanations of מצלות הסוס. The next part of the verse seems to fit only רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says huge amounts of ביזה will become holy, so it makes sense that the בית המקדש will be full of extra vessels. The other two readings (a huge ירושלים, or holy bells) say nothing about a flood of new Temple wealth. So where would all these new pots come from?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this works for one side, but...' challenge)
Basins used for the blood of קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: 'Those two' means the two OTHER opinions, רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי אלעזר. It does not mean two verses.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said
'all the spoils that Israel take'
that is why it is written:
'And the pots in the house of ה׳ shall be
like the basins before the altar.'
But according to the ones who said those other two explanations,
what is 'And the pots in the house of ה׳'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר כׇּל בִּיזָּה שֶׁבָּזְזוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the three readings of מצלות against the next verse
steps.kashyaTarget: The readings of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse describes extra Temple vessels. Only the spoils reading explains where that wealth comes from.

steps.title: The pots verse is describing something else
steps.stepSummary: According to the other two opinions, the pots verse is a separate prophecy: ישראל will become rich and donate to the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is saying a different thing: ישראל will become rich, and they will donate and bring gifts to the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The pots verse does not have to be about spoils. It can be a separate promise that the Jews will become wealthy and donate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra vessels come from voluntary donations, not from holy ביזה. So the verse fits all three opinions, and the readings of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי אלעזר still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It is saying a different matter

phrases.english: It is saying a different matter:
that Israel will become rich
and they will donate and bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the verse as a separate prophecy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pots verse must be describing holy spoils
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse describes voluntary donations from newly rich ישראל

steps.title: The 'no more כנעני' verse fits only the spoils opinion
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'there will be no more כנעני (merchant) in ה׳'s house' fits the spoils opinion. What does it mean for the other two?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who said 'spoils'. That is why it is written: 'And there shall no longer be a כנעני (merchant) in the house of ה׳ of hosts.' But according to the ones who said those other two explanations, what does 'there shall no longer be a כנעני' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second, similar challenge from the very next verse in זכריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If so much holy ביזה pours into the Temple, nobody will need to buy supplies from merchants, so 'no more merchant' makes sense. The other two opinions bring no extra Temple wealth, so why would merchants disappear?

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means 'merchant', not a Canaanite by nation

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said 'spoils';
that is why it is written:
'And there shall no longer be a merchant
in the house of ה׳ of hosts.'
But according to the ones who said those other two,
what is 'there shall no longer be a merchant'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel challenge from the next verse
steps.kashyaTarget: The readings of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No merchants are needed only if spoils supply the Temple. That works only with the spoils reading.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: כנעני means 'there is no poor person here'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה reads כנעני as אין כאן עני: there will be no poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The word means 'There is no poor person here.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers by reading the word כנעני as if it were split into אין כאן עני, 'there is no poor person here'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the other two opinions, the verse is not about merchants at all. It promises that nobody will be poor, so the Jews themselves can supply everything the Temple needs. This fits without any holy spoils.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no poor person here (a wordplay on כְּנַעֲנִי)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
'There is no poor person here.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כנעני means a merchant, which only fits the spoils reading
steps.terutzMaskana: כנעני is read as 'no poor person here', which fits every opinion
steps.whatToRemember: All three readings of מצלות הסוס survive. The surrounding verses can be explained with each one.

steps.title: How do we know כנעני can mean merchant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word כנעני can mean a merchant.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that a merchant is called כנעני?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back to ask a side question. Earlier it assumed that כנעני means 'merchant', so now it wants a source for that meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 depended on reading כנעני as 'merchant' instead of 'Canaanite'. The גמרא now wants proof that this meaning really exists in תנ״ך.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that a merchant is called כנעני?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about a word used in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that כנעני means merchant

steps.title: The verse about יהודה's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the verse 'יהודה saw the daughter of a man who was a כנעני' and asks what כנעני means there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And יהודה saw there the daughter of a man who was a כנעני.' What does כנעני mean here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse from בראשית as a possible proof. It sets up the next move by asking what the word means in that verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses כנעני to describe יהודה's father-in-law. The proof only works if כנעני here cannot mean an actual Canaanite, which the גמרא shows next.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And Judah saw there
the daughter of a man who was a כנעני.'
What is 'כנעני'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source in answer to step 22

steps.title: It cannot mean an actual Canaanite
steps.stepSummary: אברהם warned יצחק, and יצחק warned יעקב, not to marry Canaanites. Could יהודה then go and marry one?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means an actual Canaanite, is it possible? אברהם came and warned יצחק, יצחק came and warned יעקב, and יהודה would go and marry one?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the simple reading that יהודה's wife was a real Canaanite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבות strongly warned against marrying Canaanites, with each generation passing the warning on. It is unthinkable that יהודה ignored this, so כנעני in this verse must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say an actual Canaanite,

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר בָּא אַבְרָהָם וְהִזְהִיר אֶת יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: is it possible? Abraham came and warned Isaac,
Isaac came and warned Jacob,
and Judah would go and marry one?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the literal reading of the verse in step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The literal meaning 'Canaanite' in this verse
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would mean יהודה ignored his family's repeated warning

steps.title: ריש לקיש: She was a merchant's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says she was a merchant's daughter, and proves that כנען means merchant from הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: She was the daughter of a merchant, as it is written: 'כנען (the merchant), in his hand are scales of deceit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן לקיש explains that יהודה's father-in-law was a merchant. He brings a verse where כנען clearly means a trader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הושע, כנען holds cheating scales, which is a picture of a dishonest trader. That proves the word can mean 'merchant'. This answers step 22 and also solves the problem raised in step 24.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
the daughter of a merchant man,
as it is written:
'The merchant, in his hand are scales of deceit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after the literal one was rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הושע י״ב: 'כנען with scales of deceit' describes a trader

steps.title: A second proof from ישעיה
steps.stepSummary: Another source: 'whose traders are princes, whose כנעניה are the honored of the land'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it from here: 'Whose traders are princes, whose merchants (כנעניה) are the honored of the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another verse as an alternative proof that כנען means merchant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this verse, כנעניה is used as a parallel to סוחריה, 'her traders'. Since the two words stand side by side with the same meaning, כנען must mean merchant.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces an alternative)

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
'Whose traders are princes,
whose merchants are the honored of the land.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative proof for the same point
steps.whatToRemember: כנעני can mean 'merchant'. This is proven from הושע and from ישעיה.

steps.title: Isn't ה׳ one already now?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'on that day ה׳ will be one and His name one' and asks whether He is not one now.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ה׳ shall be King over all the earth; on that day ה׳ shall be one and His name one.' Is that to say that now He is not one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new verse from the same prophecy in זכריה. It challenges what the verse seems to imply, setting up the explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says ה׳ will be one 'on that day', which sounds like He is not one today. That cannot be true, so the גמרא must explain what will be new in the future.

phrases.english: 'And ה׳ shall be King over all the earth;
on that day
ה׳ shall be one and His name one.'
Is that to say that now He is not one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new verse from the same prophecy in זכריה
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the verse in זכריה י״ד:ט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying He 'will be' one implies He is not one now, which is impossible

steps.title: In the World-to-Come there will be only one blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא explains 'ה' will be one'. Today there are two blessings for news, one for good and one for bad. In עולם הבא there will only be 'הטוב והמטיב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said: The World-to-Come is not like this world. In this world, for good news a person says 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good,' and for bad news he says 'Blessed is the true Judge.' In the World-to-Come, it will all be 'He Who is good and does good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step: if ה' is one now, what does 'on that day ה' will be one' add? רבי אחא בר חנינא explains that in the future we will praise ה' in only one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today ה' is of course one, but we relate to Him through two different blessings, because some news feels good and some feels bad. In עולם הבא everything will be clearly good, so only one blessing will be needed. That is the new 'oneness' the פסוק promises.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and does good', the blessing said on good news
'The true Judge', the blessing said on bad news

steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows where the halachos of ברכת הטוב והמטיב and ברכת דיין האמת fit into the big picture. Today we need two blessings. In the future, only one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
The World-to-Come is not like this world.

phrases.aramaic: הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, עַל בְּשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: In this world, over good news one says:
'Blessed is He Who is good and does good,'
and over bad news one says:
'Blessed is the true Judge.'
In the World-to-Come, it is all 'Who is good and does good.'
phrases.notes: Only one blessing, because there will only be good.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: לֹא כָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27 about what 'ה' will be one' means if He is already one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: 'one' means one way of blessing, not one God.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to imply that ה' is not one today.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One' means that in the future ה' will be praised with only one blessing, הטוב והמטיב.

steps.title: What does 'and His name one' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks about the second half of the פסוק, 'ושמו אחד'. Is His Name not one today?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And His name will be one.' What does 'one' mean? Is it that nowadays His name is not one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of the same פסוק and asks the same kind of question. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explained 'ה' will be one'. But the פסוק also says 'His name will be one'. Since ה' has one Name already, the גמרא asks what will change about the Name in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenge word)

phrases.english: 'And His name one.' What does 'one' mean?

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ הָאִידָּנָא לָאו שְׁמוֹ אֶחָד הוּא?
phrases.english: Is that to say that now His name is not one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ הָאִידָּנָא לָאו שְׁמוֹ אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 27, now asked about the second half of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'ושמו אחד' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If His Name is already one today, the promise that it 'will be one' seems to say nothing new.

steps.title: In the future the Name will be read as it is written
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that today the Name is written יוד-הי but read as אדנ-י. In עולם הבא it will be read just as it is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The World-to-Come is not like this world. In this world, the Name is written with יוד הי and read with אלף דלת. But in the World-to-Come it will all be one: read with יוד הי and written with יוד הי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question about 'His name will be one.' The written Name and the spoken Name will become the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today there is a gap between the Name's spelling (י-ה-ו-ה) and how we say it (אדנ-י). In the future that gap disappears. The 'oneness' of the Name means writing and reading will match.

keyTerms.meaning: The letters י-ה, the start of the four-letter Name
The letters א-ד, the start of 'אדנ-י', the way we say the Name

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of the פסוק describe the future. 'ה' will be one' means only one blessing, הטוב והמטיב. 'His name will be one' means the Name will be said exactly as it is written.
steps.confusionAlert: Neither answer means ה' is somehow 'less one' today. Both answers explain a change in how we experience Him or relate to Him, not a change in ה' Himself.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The World-to-Come is not like this world.
In this world, it is written with yud-hei
and read with alef-dalet.
phrases.notes: We say אדנ-י instead of the written Name.

phrases.english: But in the World-to-Come it is all one:

phrases.aramaic: נִקְרָא בְּיוֹד הֵי וְנִכְתַּב בְּיוֹד הֵי.
phrases.english: read with yud-hei and written with yud-hei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא כָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: 'one' means the written and spoken forms will match.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to imply the Name is not one today.
steps.terutzMaskana: Today the Name is written one way and read another. In the future it will be read as written.

steps.title: רבא wanted to teach the Name's pronunciation publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבא planned to teach the proper pronunciation of the Name in his public lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא thought to teach it in his public lecture.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story begins: רבא planned to teach publicly how to pronounce the Name. This sets up the next step, where someone objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after learning that today the Name is not said as it is written, רבא wanted to teach its pronunciation to the public. The question is whether this may be taught openly.

keyTerms.meaning: To expound it, to teach it
A public lecture, usually given before a יום טוב

phrases.english: Rava thought to expound it in the public lecture,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the pronunciation of the Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grows out of step 30's point about how the Name is pronounced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא intended to teach the Name's pronunciation publicly.

steps.title: An old man stops רבא: the Name must stay hidden
steps.stepSummary: An old man tells רבא that 'לעולם' in the פסוק is spelled 'לעלם', hinting that the Name must be hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain old man said to him: It is written 'לעלם'.
steps.whatsHappening: An old man pushes back on רבא's plan. He points to a spelling in the Torah that teaches the Name should be kept hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק 'זה שמי לעולם' (שמות ג:טו), the word is written without a vav, so it can be read 'לְעַלֵּם', 'to hide'. That spelling teaches that the Name's pronunciation must be kept concealed. So רבא should not teach it publicly.

keyTerms.meaning: To conceal, read from the spelling of 'לעולם' without a vav

steps.whatToRemember: The Name is pronounced differently from how it is written. Its real pronunciation is kept hidden, based on the spelling 'לעלם'.

phrases.english: A certain old man said to him:
'To conceal' is written.
phrases.notes: 'לעולם' is spelled without a vav, so it can be read 'לעלם', to hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's plan from step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's plan to teach the Name's pronunciation publicly.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah's spelling 'לעלם' shows that the Name must be kept hidden, not taught openly.

steps.title: רבי אבינא points out a contradiction inside one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבינא notes that 'זה שמי לעלם' (hide My Name) seems to clash with 'וזה זכרי לדור דור' (remember Me in every generation).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבינא raised a contradiction. It is written: 'This is My Name forever (לעלם, which hints at hiding),' and right after it says: 'And this is My remembrance for every generation.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבינא shows that two phrases in the same פסוק seem to pull in opposite directions. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building on the old man's hint (Step 32), 'לעלם' can be read as 'to hide,' so the Name should be concealed. But 'זכרי לדור דור' suggests the Name should be mentioned and remembered by everyone. So which is it, hidden or remembered?

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (threw two sources against each other)
My remembrance, how I am mentioned

phrases.english: Rabbi Avina raised a contradiction:
It is written: "This is My Name forever"
phrases.notes: Like we saw in step 32, 'לעלם' is spelled without a ו, which hints at 'hiding'.

phrases.english: "And this is My remembrance for every generation."
phrases.notes: This suggests the Name should be mentioned and remembered openly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the old man's reading of 'לעלם' as 'hide' and shows that it seems to clash with the next phrase.
steps.kashyaTarget: The meaning of שמות ג:טו: hidden Name or remembered Name?
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase calls for hiding the Name and the next phrase calls for mentioning it. Both cannot seem to be true.

steps.title: The Name is written one way and read another way
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא says: I am not read the way I am written. I am written יוד-הא and read אלף-דלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: I am not read the way I am written. I am written with יוד and הא, and I am read with אלף and דלת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבי אבינא's contradiction. Both phrases are true, each about a different part of the Name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שמי' (the written Name, יוד-הא) is the part that stays hidden, because we do not pronounce it. 'זכרי' (how the Name is mentioned out loud, אדנ-י, starting with אלף-דלת) is used in every generation. This matches רב נחמן בר יצחק's idea in Step 30 that today the Name is written one way and read another.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
The first letters of the written Name (שם הוי״ה)
The first letters of the spoken Name, אדנ-י

steps.whatToRemember: 'Hidden' refers to the written Name (יוד-הא), which we never pronounce. 'Remembered' refers to the spoken form (אדנ-י), which we use all the time.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Not as I am written am I read.
I am written with yod and heh,
and I am read with alef and dalet.
phrases.notes: This refers to the pronounced form אדנ-י.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: לֹא כְּשֶׁאֲנִי נִכְתָּב, אֲנִי נִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two phrases into two different things: the written Name versus the spoken Name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say the same Name is both hidden and publicized.
steps.terutzMaskana: The written Name (יוד-הא) is hidden. The spoken Name (אלף-דלת) is the one remembered in every generation.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק אלו עוברין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק אלו עוברין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'אלו עוברין'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the third פרק of מסכת פסחים. It is not part of the argument. It is a closing statement before a new פרק begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses a hope to come back and learn this פרק again. The sugya about the Name is now finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a פרק)
The name of the third פרק of פסחים

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Eilu Ovrin"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the entire פרק after the final אגדה.

steps.title: Working on ערב פסח depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: where people are used to doing מלאכה on ערב פסח until חצות, one may do it. Where they are used to not doing it, one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: In a place where people are used to doing work on ערב פסח until midday, they do work. In a place where people are used to not doing work, they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק, מקום שנהגו, opens with a משנה. It teaches that doing מלאכה on the morning of ערב פסח depends on the local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not state a fixed rule from the תורה for the morning of ערב פסח. Instead, it lets the local מנהג decide: if the town works, you may work, and if the town refrains, you must refrain. The time limit 'עד חצות' covers the morning only.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people have the custom

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the foundation for the whole פרק, which deals with the power of local מנהג in halacha.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A place where they were accustomed
to do work on Passover eve
until midday: they do it.
A place where they were accustomed not to do work
they do not do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand-new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether one may do מלאכה on ערב פסח until חצות follows the local מנהג.

steps.title: A traveler keeps the stricter customs of both places
steps.stepSummary: Someone who travels between a place that works and a place that does not must keep the חומרות of both the place he left and the place he went to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone goes from a place where people work to a place where they do not, or from a place where they do not work to a place where they do, we place on him the strict rules of the place he left and the strict rules of the place he went to.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the case of a traveler who moves between towns with different customs. He must follow whichever custom is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The traveler takes along the strictness of his home town, and he also takes on the strictness of his new town. In practice, both directions lead to the same result: he does not do מלאכה. The custom that forbids work always wins.

keyTerms.meaning: The strict rules of a place

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that moving to a working town lets him work. Even going from a non-working town to a working town, he keeps his home town's strictness and may not work.
steps.whatToRemember: A traveler is bound by the stricter custom of both his home town and the town he goes to.

phrases.english: One who goes from a place where they work
to a place where they do not work,
or from a place where they do not work
to a place where they work:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין עָלָיו חוּמְרֵי מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּצָא מִשָּׁם
phrases.english: we place upon him the stringencies of the place he left
and the stringencies of the place he went to.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוֹלֵךְ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the local-custom rule of Step 36 to a person who moves between places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler must keep the stringencies of both the place he left and the place he arrived in.
